actual_outputs.answer: No, payroll access will not definitely be restored within 30 minutes. The 30-minute target is an initial response time for payroll-blocking MFA incidents, not a guarantee for restoration, as it depends on several factors including identity verification and provider availability [SEC-17::service-targets-and-uncertainty][OPS-09::employee-communication].

inputs.question: My phone was stolen and I received an unexpected MFA prompt. What must happen?

actual_outputs.answer: If you received an unexpected MFA prompt after your phone was stolen, you must report the incident immediately. The old authenticator registration will be revoked once your identity is verified, and the Help Desk will record the loss [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices]. Additionally, since you reported an unexpected MFA prompt, security escalation is mandatory [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices]. Be sure to contact the Help Desk through an approved corporate channel to initiate this process [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow].

The Help Desk records the loss in the ticket and advises the employee to report suspected device compromise to Security Operations. inputs.question: What information must the Help Desk record in an MFA recovery ticket?

actual_outputs.answer:
The Help Desk must record the following information in an MFA recovery ticket:

- Employee identifier
- Corporate contact channel
- Affected payroll function
- Deadline if any
- Device-loss status
- Verification methods attempted
- Verification outcome
- Old-authenticator revocation status
- Re-enrolment outcome
- Retrieved policy version
- Every escalation made

It is important to note that passwords, OTP values, full identity numbers, banking PINs, or recovery secrets must not be included in the ticket [OPS-09::required-ticket-fields]. Additionally, the old authenticator registration must be revoked as soon as identity is verified if a device is reported lost or stolen [SEC-17::lost-or-stolen-devices].
